facts.statement: Fossils of Wintonotitan were first discovered in 1974 by Keith Watts.
facts.quote: Fossils that are now known under the name Wintonotitan were first found in 1974 by Keith Watts.

facts.statement: The type specimen QMF 7292 was formally established as the holotype for Wintonotitan in 2009 by Scott Hocknull and colleagues.
facts.quote: QMF 7292 was established as the type specimen of Wintonotitan in 2009 by Scott Hocknull and colleagues.

facts.statement: Researchers suggested that the previously named species Austrosaurus mckillopi is a nomen dubium and differs only slightly from the holotype of Wintonotitan wattsii.
facts.quote: Hocknull suggested that Austrosaurus mckillopi differed only slightly from the QMF 7292, the holotype of Wintonotitan wattsii, and should be considered a nomen dubium.

facts.statement: Wintonotitan is known from partial postcranial remains.
facts.quote: It is known from partial postcranial remains.

facts.statement: The holotype fossils were found in sandstone interpreted as a river point bar.
facts.quote: QMF 7292 was found in sandstone interpreted as a point bar of a river.

facts.statement: Like other sauropods, Wintonotitan was a large quadrupedal herbivore measuring around 16 meters in length.
facts.quote: Como otros saurópodos, Wintonotitan fue un gran cuadrúpedo herbívoro que medía alrededor de 16 metros de largo.

facts.statement: In its 2009 description, Wintonotitan was classified as a non-titanosaurian titanosauriform sauropod.
facts.quote: In their 2009 description, Hocknull et al. found Wintonotitan to be a non-titanosaurian titanosauriform sauropod in their phylogenetic analyses.

facts.statement: Wintonotitan lived during the Cenomanian to Turonian stages, approximately 100.5 to 89.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Turonian (100.5 to 89.8 million years ago)

facts.statement: A second specimen consisting of isolated tail vertebrae was found at Chorregan.
facts.quote: Un segundo espécimen, QMF10916, consiste de vértebras caudales aisladas, encontradas en Chorregan.

facts.statement: Wintonotitan bones can be distinguished from Diamantinasaurus bones because they are not as robust.
facts.quote: Los huesos de Wintonotitan se distingue de Diamantinasurus debido a que los de Wintonotitan no son tan robustos.

rejected.statement: A 2024 analysis by Beeston et al. recovered Wintonotitan within the Diamantinasauria clade as the sister taxon to Titanosauria.
rejected.quote: In their 2024 review and analysis of sauropod fossils from the Winton Formation, Beeston et al. ... recovered the clade as the sister taxon to the Titanosauria within the Somphospondyli.
rejected.reason: quote not found verbatim in the source

rejected.statement: The phylogenetic placement of Wintonotitan and related sauropods from the Winton Formation has been contentious among researchers.
rejected.quote: The phylogenetic placement of the contemporary sauropods in the Winton Formation ... has been contentious.
